title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Azerbaijan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Azerbaijan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Azerbaijan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a death occurs in Azerbaijan, statutory duties begin immediately with medical certification, civil status registration, and pension or allowance notifications, while estate succession runs under a six-month notarial window [1] [2] [7]. We have set out the practical order of steps below, including apostille rules where documents must be presented abroad [9].

steps.title: Immediate medical confirmation and death registration
steps.html:
• Obtain the medical death certificate: If the death occurred in a hospital or clinic, the attending facility issues Form AZS-106 (medical certificate of death) [11] and transmits the record electronically; for deaths at home or sudden deaths, contact the Ministry of Emergency Situations 112 Hotline (112 or 103 ambulance) so forensic and emergency authorities can confirm cause of death and issue the medical certificate [1] [12].
  • Register the death at ASAN Service or the Registration Department: Under the Family Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan and Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan civil registration rules, a relative, authorized representative, or housing authority submits the medical death certificate, the deceased's identity document (and residence permit if a foreign or stateless resident), and any military service card to an ASAN Service center or district Registration Department [1] [6] [7].
  • Deadlines and fees: Initial civil death registration and issuance of the first death certificate at ASAN Service centers and Ministry of Justice Registration Departments are free of charge; standard reporting should be completed promptly (typically within 10 days of death or discovery) [6] [7]. Request multiple official copies if banks, employers, or consular missions need originals [11].

steps.title: Funeral, cremation, and cross-border repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial arrangements: Confirm municipal cemetery allocation and obtain transport clearance using the medical certificate of death and civil death certificate before burial [7] [11]. Cremation facilities are not routinely available inside Azerbaijan, so families seeking cremation generally arrange international repatriation [11].
  • Repatriation abroad: If remains are being transferred outside Azerbaijan, obtain an embalming and sealing certificate, a non-infectious disease clearance from sanitary-epidemiological authorities, customs export clearance, and consular coordination [11].
  • Apostille for cross-border use: Azerbaijan has been a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention since 2 March 2005 [9]. Official civil registry death certificates and notarial succession documents are apostilled via the Ministry of Justice (or submitted through ASAN Service Center No. 5 / Ministry of Foreign Affairs depending on issuing body) for a state duty of 10 AZN under Article 13-1 of the Law on State Duty [8] [9].

steps.title: Lump-sum funeral allowance and social insurance claims
steps.html:
• Who pays the funeral grant: The State Social Protection Fund (MLSPP) and DOST Agency administer one-time funeral allowances under the Law on Labour Pensions and the Law on Social Benefits [4] [5] [10] [14].
  • Automated assignment and rates: Effective 1 May 2026, the one-time funeral allowance is assigned automatically in the electronic system upon civil death registration where the deceased received state social benefits, unemployment insurance, or compulsory social insurance (600 AZN), or three times the minimum monthly labour pension for labour pensioners [10].
  • Manual backup application: Where automated assignment does not trigger (for example, due to missing family or expense data), the person who paid funeral expenses can apply without any statutory time limit at the State Social Protection Fund, a DOST Center, or a regional branch with an ID card, death certificate, municipal burial confirmation, and Ministry of Justice registration extract [10].

steps.title: Succession, notaries, and the six-month deadline
steps.html:
• Open the inheritance file within six months: Under Articles 1145 and 1246 of the Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Law on Notariat, succession opens on the date of death, and heirs must formally accept the estate at a licensed notary office (including notarial desks at ASAN Service centers) within six months [2] [3] [7].
  • Order of statutory heirs and wills: First-order statutory heirs under Article 1159 are children, surviving spouse, and parents in equal shares unless altered by a notarized will executed under Article 1166 [2].
  • Inheritance certificate and fees: ASAN Service notaries issue a certificate of right to inheritance by law after checking the register of wills; statutory state fees are 25 AZN for statutory heirs in order of priority and 50 AZN for other persons [7]. Heirs should also check bank accounts, real estate registry extracts, and outstanding debts, as inherited liability is capped at estate value [2].

steps.title: Tax treatment and closing accounts
steps.html:
• Inheritance tax exemption: Azerbaijan levies no standalone inheritance tax; under Article 102.1.3.2 of the Tax Code, property and gifts inherited from family members are exempt from personal income tax [13].
  • Deceased taxpayer liabilities: Under Article 80 of the Tax Code, unpaid tax liabilities of the deceased pass proportionally to heirs up to the value of inherited property as of receipt, or are written off if no heirs exist [13].
  • Notify banks, utilities, and employers: Present notarized or apostilled inheritance certificates and death certificates to close or transfer bank accounts, terminate utilities, and claim final unpaid wages or private insurance payouts [7] [11].

closingQuestion: Which city or district did your family member live in, and do you need to use the Azerbaijani death certificate or inheritance papers in another country?

contacts.name: ASAN Service
contacts.note: Call center 108 handles inquiries on free civil death registration, notarial inheritance certificates, and apostille submissions.

contacts.name: Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan
contacts.note: Oversees civil status registration departments, licensed notaries, and apostille issuance (10 AZN state duty) for court, civil registry, and notarial acts.

contacts.name: State Social Protection Fund (MLSPP) and DOST Agency
contacts.note: Call center 142 handles lump-sum funeral allowances (600 AZN / 3x minimum pension), automated payout verification, and survivor pensions.

contacts.name: Ministry of Emergency Situations 112 Hotline
contacts.note: 24/7 emergency coordination hotline (also connects to 103 ambulance services for home death attendance).
